summary: Audit export: timestamp normalization drift and HEC field mapping mismatch causing SIEM correlation gaps for Northbridge Bank
description:
Issue summary: Northbridge Bank reports missing event correlation in Splunk HEC and their SIEM analytic rules failing to match sessions. They see inconsistent 'auth.user' and 'user_email' attributes across our audit-export batches and a ~2 minute timestamp skew between Redwood's audit timestamps and the customer's SIEM ingest time.

Impact: Correlation rules used by the customer's SOC are dropping 15-25% of activity windows (estimated) for high-risk user sessions during business hours. This is a compliance risk for their upcoming audit window and causing elevated support tickets from their SOC.

Background: Customer onboarded with Private deployment (VPC) in us-east. They consume audit exports via Splunk HEC endpoint configured with Redwood's audit-forwarder. They also asked for RFC3339 timestamps in UTC but some downstream records appear in local timezone offsets and a subset of events drop the 'auth.user' field in favor of 'actor_identity' which their correlation pipeline does not map.

Observed behaviour:
- Batches delivered via HEC show event._time values that differ from the Redwood 'timestamp' field by ~120 seconds for a sample of events (2026-03-09 09:12:xx).
- auth.user sometimes absent; actor_identity present instead for same event id.
- Customer's SPL queries return fewer results compared to direct API lookups.

Expected behaviour: All audit records exported to customer's SIEM should contain canonical fields (timestamp in RFC3339 UTC in 'timestamp', and canonical identity in 'auth.user') and stable field names across batches.

Attachments referenced by customer: sample_event_ids: ["evt_8c9a1f","evt_8c9a56","evt_8c9b02"], exported_batch_ids: ["batch-20260309-0910-01","batch-20260309-0915-01"].
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer queries Splunk HEC for batch batch-20260309-0910-01 using the provided HEC token
2) Filter events where event.id == evt_8c9a1f and compare event.timestamp vs _time (Splunk ingestion time)
3) Inspect fields auth.user, actor_identity, user_email on the same event payload
4) Run Redwood Console -> Exports -> Audit -> download raw JSON for corresponding batch and compare field presence
5) Reproduce sampling across a 1 hour window to measure skew rate
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:45 - Triage: confirmed customer sample; initial hypothesis: exporter batching causing re-ordering and ingestion timestamp assigned by Splunk differs due to network buffering
03/10 11:12 - SRE (Marco): observed that our forwarder adds a pipeline 'processed_at' header but should not alter the payload 'timestamp'. Need to verify timezone handling in exporter v2.3.1

03/10 13:30 - Data team: field normalization rule recently added (PR 8245) renames 'identity' -> 'actor_identity' for internal consumers; mapping to 'auth.user' for SIEM was missed in that rule. Potential root cause for missing auth.user
03/10 15:05 - Correlation with INT-4421: internal task to roll patch to fix field mapping and add timezone normalization to HEC exporter

03/11 09:00 - Reproduction: local staging forwarder using same config reproduces timestamp delta when network delay injected; suggests combined effects of buffering and Splunk assigning _time on ingest.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:02 - Aisha Patel (Support): Thanks for the report. We've opened investigation and queued SRE. Can you confirm whether your Splunk HEC endpoint has 'useTimeFromEvent' enabled?
2026-03-10 10:20 - Northbridge SOC (customer): Confirmed HEC is configured with default behavior (useTimeFromEvent=false) — they rely on our exporter 'timestamp' field.

2026-03-10 11:20 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): We see two issues: (1) field rename in recent normalization PR missed a SIEM mapping, (2) some HEC consumers are not honoring event timestamp if useTimeFromEvent=false and Splunk assigns _time at ingest. Working on mitigation.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Aisha Patel (Support): Notified customer that we have a short-term workaround and a backfill plan. Customer requests an ETA for patch and confirmation that historical events can be re-exported for last 7 days.

2026-03-11 09:05 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): ETA for hotfix to field mapping and timestamp normalization: 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC. Backfill plan requires export job; will require a maintenance window and signed consent from customer.
resolution: Planned actions: 1) Hotfix PR to exporter to restore SIEM mapping (map actor_identity -> auth.user when actor_identity present) and enforce RFC3339 UTC 'timestamp' in payload (PR referenced: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8245). 2) Deploy hotfix to staging and run integration test with customer's HEC config. 3) Coordinate maintenance window with Northbridge for backfill export for last 7 days; provide sample proof-of-concept export for 1-hour slice for validation. 4) Long-term: add exporter config flag 'force_event_ts' and a console validation step that alerts when Splunk HEC is configured to override incoming timestamps. Status: hotfix in code review, scheduled deploy 2026-03-12, customer notified. Follow-ups: create INT ticket for exporter config validation (INT-4421) and update Playbook.
follow_up_tasks: Create INT runbook entry for SIEM timestamp normalization checks
Schedule backfill and produce proof-of-delivery manifest (HMAC) for exported batches
Add new console alert when export field schema drifts
Confirm backfill completion and update customer with manifest and MD5 checksums
